questions.stem: A team already writes its orchestration as Python DAGs and wants Fabric to run them as a managed service. Another team wants to orchestrate without writing code. Which pairing fits?

options.text: Pipelines for the Python DAGs, and an Apache Airflow job for the team that wants no code
An Apache Airflow job for the Python DAGs, and pipelines for the team that wants no code
An Apache Airflow job for both teams, since the job converts DAGs into a drag-and-drop canvas
A Spark job definition for the Python DAGs, and a Dataflow Gen2 for the team that wants no code

questions.explanation: Apache Airflow jobs build and run Python-based DAGs as a managed service, for people who prefer writing code. If you'd rather not write code, pipelines offer a no-code way to handle orchestration.

questions.stem: An Apache Airflow job created on Airflow 2.10.5 must move to a newer Airflow version. What's the supported way?

options.text: Turn on autoscale, which upgrades the job to the newest Airflow version when it scales
Install the newer Airflow as a private package requirement in the existing job
Change the version in the existing job's settings; it restarts on the new version
Create a new Apache Airflow job with the version you want, and move the DAGs to it

questions.explanation: Changing the Apache Airflow version within an existing job isn't supported: create a new job with the version you want.

questions.stem: Which two of these does an Apache Airflow job support, according to its feature list?

options.text: Running the DAGs as a Dataflow Gen2 refresh on a schedule
Installing a private package as a requirement
Converting each DAG into a pipeline item in the workspace
Git sync, so the job's DAGs come from a Git repository

questions.explanation: The feature list includes Git sync, installing a private package as a requirement, pause and resume time to live, autoscale and high availability.

questions.stem: Nobody runs DAGs at night, and the team wants the Airflow environment to stop using compute when idle. Which feature is meant for that?

options.text: High availability, which moves the job to a standby
Git sync, which pulls DAGs only when they change
Pause and resume with a time to live (TTL)
Autoscale, which grows the workers during production spikes

questions.explanation: The feature list names pause and resume time to live (TTL); autoscale handles execution spikes and high availability handles outages.
